A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including Appendices A–C in v2. Material moved from the main text into appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 contains conceptual illustrations, descriptions of cited methods, theoretical convergence summaries and a dataset catalogue. It reports no original experimental or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: Figures 4 and 7 report solution distributions from the authors' LSMOP1 experiment. Appendix B explicitly states that each algorithm was run for 5000 iterations.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an original optimizer or model. V2 adds coverage of UPGrad and corrects mathematical descriptions of existing algorithms; these do not establish a change to a method developed by this work.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on the two-objective LSMOP1 synthetic optimization problem. The datasets catalogued in v1 remain listed in v2, with their descriptions moved to Appendix C; they are not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: A new illustrative LSMOP1 comparison evaluates PMTL, EPO, GradHV, MOO-SVGD, MGDA, PMGDA, UMOD and Smooth Tchebycheff. V1 discusses these approaches but contains no corresponding experimental comparison. The addition is confined to this single example.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces a common budget of 5000 iterations per algorithm for the new LSMOP1 experiment, with solution distributions displayed against the true Pareto front and preference directions. This is a new evaluation procedure, not a revision of an existing experiment.

E4.justification: Figures 4 and 7 add a small visual case study examining solution diversity and preference alignment under different optimization approaches. Appendix B contrasts clustering, approximate alignment and exact alignment. No ablation or robustness sweep is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The solution points in v2 are not identified as repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds eight solution-distribution plots and associated findings: MGDA has poor diversity, PMTL lacks exact alignment, EPO and PMGDA align with preferences, and GradHV and MOO-SVGD produce diverse solutions. These are newly reported outcomes, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the hypervolume ascent update from subtracting to adding the gradient step. V1 Equation 44 becomes v2 Equation 40 with the smoothing factor correctly multiplying the gradient difference in MoCo. The main theorem and tabulated convergence bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claim of a comprehensive survey covering gradient-based MOO algorithms, theory and applications, organized around single, finite and infinite solution sets. The new experiment does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds explicit discussion of parallel computation and memory efficiency for independent preference subproblems, together with their inability to share information. Section 4.2 also revises the MosT explanation from uniform-distribution weighting to assigning objectives to solutions through optimal transport.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new experiment's 5000-iteration budget, explicitly identifies Panacea's learnable matrices and scalars, and updates LibMTL's reported coverage from over 19 methods to 24. The library links and relocated dataset specifications remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds UPGrad, MOEA/D, the LSMOP benchmark source, additional hypervolume and MORL references, and two physics-informed neural network works. Several hypervolume and UCB background references are removed. Other apparent additions, including stochastic methods in the taxonomy, were already discussed in v1.

P1.justification: V2 broadly edits and condenses technical explanations, substantially shortens Section 8 by moving dataset descriptions to Appendix C, moves the Pareto illustration discussion to Appendix A, and converts Section 9's numbered subsections into paragraph headings. Together these constitute substantial editorial reorganization, although the main survey outline remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds an overview diagram and two four-panel experimental figures, expands and reformats the taxonomy, rearranges the network diagrams from stacked to side-by-side panels, and moves and annotates the Pareto illustration. Table 2 changes from a full-width display to a compact single-column table with an expanded caption.

improvement.justification: The corrected hypervolume and MoCo equations resolve concrete mathematical errors, while the overview diagram and LSMOP1 case study improve the survey's explanatory value. Literature and resource updates add modest utility. The experiment remains a single synthetic illustration with sparse implementation details and no uncertainty reporting, so the overall gain is limited.
